audio_caption: The audio clip begins with a male speaker outlining the premise of his commentary, mentioning answering internet search questions about architects and architecture using Google. He clarifies the method, typing queries such as "do architects blank" and answering top Google search results. Proceeding with the first question, he asks "do architects do math?"

The audio clip begins with a male speaker affirming that architects do math, emphasizing this point and suggesting practice for those considering the field. He expresses that math is a "practicable and masterable skill". Next, he poses the question "do architects need to be good at drawing?".

The clip starts with a male speaker explaining why architects need to be good at drawing, which has something to do with architecture school. He then asks, "do architects earn a lot of money," in a curious tone. The speaker acknowledges it's a Schrodinger's Cat of architectural questions and some architects earn a lot of money while others don't. He compares architects to actors, highlighting the existence of "starchitects" who are stars in their field. He further describes some architects as unknown and earning an honest living. He shifts to asking if architects and engineers work together.

The clip starts with a male speaker addressing a controversial question about architects and engineers. He notes a misconception about their relationship before stating architects love engineers but engineers probably hate architects. He confirms that architects and engineers do work together and should collaborate. He then pivots to the next question about architects' travel habits, explaining that he doesn't travel much but knows architects who have projects all over the country. He ends the clip by moving on to the next phrase to search.

The clip starts with a man's voice introducing the topic of architects, inquiring, "Can architects be rich?" He speaks in a clear, inquisitive tone, asserting his opinion that they can be rich, though not to the level of someone like Elon Musk, solely from architecture. He then transitions to the next question: "Can architects have tattoos?" He questions why not, noting the public image of architects as clean-cut professionals. He adds that perceptions are changing, suggesting a future with heavily tattooed architects. The man's tone shifts towards casual and playful. He then gets back on track, prompting the next question: "Can architects sign structural drawings?"

The audio clip features a single male speaker with a conversational tone discussing the abilities and limitations of architects. He states, "The answer to this question is no. Architects cannot sign structural drawings." He further elaborates on the distinction between architects and structural engineers, explaining their respective roles in design and authorization. The speaker then shifts to the topic of interior design, mentioning a historical change in the Philippines that now disallows architects from practicing interior design. Subsequently, the speaker confirms that architects can work from home, describing his personal routine of site visits followed by home-based detail work and 3D modeling. Finally, he poses the question of whether architects can advertise.

The clip begins with a man speaking with a conversational tone, discussing a "code of ethics" in the Philippines that restricts architects from advertising through traditional media, but questions if this rule applies to social media. He asks, "Are architects blank?". A male voice briefly interjects.

The clip features one male speaker discussing the demand for architects. His tone is conversational and informative. He mentions that while they are not in high demand in the Philippines, they are sought after in developing countries like Singapore and Dubai. He also notes that in third-world countries like the Philippines, architects are often considered a "luxury profession" affordable only to the wealthy.

The clip features a male speaker exploring the question of whether architects are artists. He says he "would like to think so" and jokes about classifying himself. He then delves into the question of whether architects are engineers, stating it's controversial but affirming that "architecture actually belongs under the field of engineering" and that "architects are engineers." He continues by humorously expressing surprise at the question of whether architects are happy and asking "who would ask this question, man?" before again stating "I would like to."

The audio clip begins with a man speaking casually, inquiring about the happiness of architects and considering asking his classmates about their job satisfaction. He then asks a question, "Why do architects wear black?". He goes on to say he wears black because it suits him and hides stains. He says it is one of the upsides of wearing black shirts, but otherwise a personal preference. Lastly, he asks "Why do architects need a license?".

The clip opens with a single male speaker explaining that one does not need a license, but an "architectural license" is required to be an architect. Continuing in an informational tone, the speaker then discusses why architects make models, mentioning personal experience using scale models for client presentations, particularly when computer renderings are insufficient. The speaker states that they generally avoid making scale models because they are costly and potentially dangerous. The clip ends with the speaker asking "Why do arc-".

The audio clip begins with a single male speaker wondering aloud why architects utilize copper roofs and explaining that architects use such materials for aesthetic and sustainable reasons. He then questions why architects use blueprints, clarifies that blueprints are no longer commonly used due to the advancement of printing technology and harmful chemicals. The tone is informational and casual. Background noises are absent.

The clip begins with a male speaker explaining why architects use different types of lines in their drawings, such as dotted or dashed lines, to differentiate various aspects of the drawings, particularly to represent hidden geometries, and to prevent the drawings from being confusing. The speaker then asks why architects sketch, and proceeds to state that he sketches to come up with ideas.

The clip begins with a speaker, male, describing his artistic process, emphasizing sketching as a low-effort and enjoyable step leading to a finalized drawing, his speaking tone casual. There are no other sounds present in the audio.

The clip starts with a single male speaker asking "How do architects?" and quickly rephrases the question as "How do architects earn money?" He explains that architects earn money by "getting clients," leading him to the subsequent question of how they acquire those clients. The speaker continues, referencing a previous discussion about architects not being allowed to advertise, and notes they rely on word of mouth. Acknowledging the changes in the media landscape, he mentions that Instagram, YouTube, and Facebook now offer avenues to showcase their work and potentially find clients.

The clip begins with a male speaker discussing how architects design houses, mentioning that it's a "very complicated" process that starts with "sketching" and includes columns, floor plans, and different approaches. He adds that he'll cover it in a future video, concluding that architects design houses with "our big brains," spoken in a somewhat comedic tone. Laughter follows the speech.

The audio clip starts with a male speaker answering a question about how architects and engineers work together. He describes a collaborative design process where he provides an architectural design for the engineers to analyze structurally, and then they send back a structural design. The speaker characterizes it as a back-and-forth process of designing a structure.

A male speaker begins, explaining how architects charge, stating they take "10% of the total project cost" in the Philippines, delivered in a straightforward tone. The clip includes background noise of an unspecified nature with consistent low volume throughout the speech.

The clip begins with a male speaker explaining the financial process of paying an architect, by saying, "Let's say the project costs 10 million Simoleons, then the architect is going to be paid 10% of that, which is 1 million Simoleons. That is how architects charge." The speaker then asks questions regarding architects: "What do architects..." followed by "what do architects do?" He answers his own questions, "We draw a ton of designs, build buildings." The speaker then asks what architects wear, mentioning that they wear black. He continues to ask what architects major in and answers: "architectural design subjects". The man proceeds to ask and answer, "What do architects do daily? We go to the site, we design, meet with the client." The clip ends with the speaker saying: "What do architects wear to work?" He explains that this depends on the architectural firm and that some require formal attire.

The audio clip begins with an individual speaking in a casual, conversational tone about architects and their attire when meeting clients. He mentions wearing T-shirts to work, and transitions to concluding a journey into the wide world of the interwebs, thanking listeners and saying he will see them in the next video. The audio ends with him saying "flying peace" followed by a brief whooshing sound effect.
